entry.title: We built an AI-powered scout for open source. Meet OpenScOut.
entry.summary:
We built OpenScOut because finding a good open-source project shouldn't be harder than contributing to one
If you've ever tried to make your first (or fiftieth) open-source contribution, you know the drill. You find a repository that looks interesting. You open the issues tab hoping for a "good first issue." The last commit was over a year ago. The maintainer hasn't responded in months. You close the tab and go back to scrolling GitHub. After a while, "I'll contribute to open source someday" quietly becomes another unfinished goal. We got tired of that experience, so we started building OpenScOut—a platform that helps developers discover active, beginner-friendly, and well-maintained open-source projects. Finding a project isn't difficult. Finding one that's active, welcoming, and worth investing your time in is. Most developers only realize a repository is inactive after they've already spent time understanding the codebase. Search repositories using filters like language, stars, forks, and recent activity to find projects that match your skills. Analyze any GitHub repository and receive an A–F contribution readiness score based on project health, maintainer responsiveness, issue quality, activity, and more. Browse Google Summer of Code organizations and project ideas from one place instead of jumping across multiple websites. We believe developers should spend more time building and contributing than deciding whether a repository is worth contributing to. OpenScOut is still in active development, and we're building it alongside the community. If you've ever struggled to find the right open-source project, we'd love your feedback. We'll be sharing development updates, new features, and the launch over on LinkedIn. 👉 Follow the journey here: Follow OpenScOut on LinkedIn If you have ideas, feature requests, or want early access, leave a comment below—we'd love to hear from you. Building in public, one repo at a time. 🚀

entry.summary:
The 3am page that defines your career
At 3am, an availability zone goes dark. If your system is well-designed, nothing happens, traffic shifts, replicas take over, and you sleep through it. If it isn't, you wake up to a dead service, a CEO asking "how long until we're back," and a second question that's even worse: "how much data did we lose?" entry.title: Automatic Error Recovery in AI Agent Networks
entry.summary:
In a single-agent system, failure is simple: the agent errors, you retry. In multi-agent systems, failure is a graph problem. Agent A: ✅ Success Agent B: ❌ Timeout (depends on A) Agent C: ❌ Skipped (depends on B) Agent D: ❌ Partial data (depends on C)
One timeout propagates through the entire pipeline. Without recovery, your system is fragile. AgentForge implements 3 recovery layers: @retry(max_attempts=3, backoff=exponential(base=2, max=60)) def agent_call(params): return llm.invoke(params)
If an agent fails 5 times in 10 minutes, we stop calling it and return a degraded response: { "status": "degraded", "agent": "market_data", "fallback": "cached_data", "warning": "Real-time data unavailable, using 15-min delayed feed" }
When a critical agent fails, the orchestrator can re-plan: Skip the failed step if non-critical Substitute with a backup agent Halt and alert with full context trace Last month, our market data API went down during trading hours. Here's what happened: 14:32 — Market data agent timeout (Layer 1: 3 retries failed) 14:33 — Circuit breaker opened for market data agent 14:33 — Pipeline automatically switched to cached data + warning flag 14:35 — Full report generated with "delayed data" disclaimer 15:00 — Market data API recovered, circuit breaker closed automatically Zero manual intervention. Zero missed reports. If your multi-agent system can't handle one agent failing, it's not production-ready. AgentForge makes this the default, not an afterthought. https://github.com/agentforge-cyber/agentforge-mvp Posted on 2026-07-16 by the AgentForge team.
